analysis:
All three changed files are test-only under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. They add SelectedModelRecoveryVictimTests.swift, a ScriptedCounter helper and superLoads counter in UnreclaimableLoadMemoryFixture.swift, a residentBytes switch that gives Super its own scripted bytes, and a shutdown-liveness test in ProviderLifecycleTests.swift. No production source changed, so no runtime behavior changes for any threat-model asset or trust boundary.

The tests use temp directories, inert stub engines, scripted memory and loopback placeholder URLs (ws://127.0.0.1:0/unused). They contain no real secrets, keys, network I/O or attestation material. ScriptedCounter is @unchecked Sendable but lock-protected, and it is used only in tests.

The lifecycle test (ProviderLifecycleTests.swift ~220-243) asserts that shutdown does not hang on a slot whose unload never completes. This is consistent with the availability concerns (T-029, T-046-style stalled-shutdown and drain behavior) and documents the intended behavior.

The recovery tests document Autopilot victim rules (dwell, idle, lease, pin, stale-selection protection) that bear on A-018 serving availability and T-029. They only check intended behavior. I could not review the production recovery or shutdownBeforeRegistration code, which is outside the supplied evidence. Whether production matches these test expectations is a question for any review that covers the paired production change, if one exists. Nothing here shows a security regression.
